title: Staged Shepherding Breaker: per-tenant & per-model circuit with safe fallback choreography
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: During regional spikes or noisy tenants we see cascading latency and token-based cost escalations when model backends are saturated. Existing coarse global fuses either take too long to react or harm unaffected tenants and models. We need a fine-grained, SLO-aligned mechanism that: 1) detects degraded dependency behavior at multiple scopes (dependency, model, tenant), 2) transitions traffic through staged degradation (soft-shed -> hard-trip -> cool-down), and 3) routes safely to fallback paths (lighter model variant, cached response, or degraded feature) without violating overall customer SLAs.

This ticket implements the runtime orchestrator and control-plane config for "staged shepherding breakers" (SSB): per-dependency + per-model + per-tenant layered breakers that share signals but make local trip decisions. The orchestrator exposes: declarative breaker profiles, runtime trip calculator, telemetry exports, and a policy engine for fallback selection. The aim is predictable, observable, and reversible degradations with automated rollback if quality regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: SSB control-plane accepts breaker profiles and persists them (api + console).
Runtime evaluates breaker state per request and annotates traces with reason_code and state (OK/Soft/Tripped/Cooling).
Safe fallback selection: at least two fallback strategies available per model (quantized variant, cached-prefix, or placeholder response). Fallback chosen meets configured downstream SLO constraints.
End-to-end tests simulate tenant spike and demonstrate bounded error-rate and <5% downstream QoR regression when fallback engaged.
Dashboards show per-tenant and per-model trip history, and a canary run shows no customer-visible incidents during rollout.
design_decisions: Scope: breakers are evaluation-scoped in order: tenant > model > dependency. A hard trip at a lower scope (tenant) can preempt higher-scope decisions to protect the host infra.

Signal sources: 50th/95th/99th latency, per-second error rate, token-per-request surge, and KV-cache miss rate. Use exponentially-weighted moving averages (EWMA) with short (30s) and long (5m) windows.
Two-tier trip model: SOFT (early-warning, apply CPU-friendly work-stealing such as reduced batch sizes or passive shedding) and HARD (active reroute to fallback).
Fallback hierarchy: quantized model variant -> shorter max_tokens -> cached-prefix response -> application-level degraded feature. Each fallback is annotated and meter-counted.
Open-telemetry: include breaker_state and fallback_id on spans; emit breaker events to the metrics pipeline for alerting and postmortem.
trip_thresholds: Soft-trip (per-tenant): 95th latency > 450ms for 30s EWMA OR error-rate > 1.5% over 30s -> mark SOFT. Action: reduce batch window by 25%, apply prioritized queueing for payment-tiered tenants.

Hard-trip (per-tenant): 99th latency > 900ms for 60s EWMA OR token-throughput increase > 4x baseline sustained 60s -> mark TRIPPED. Action: route 30% of traffic to fallback immediately, schedule further ramp to 70% over 2 mins if signal persists.
Per-model soft-trip: 95th latency > model_profile.p95 * 1.4 for 30s -> SOFT. Per-model hard-trip: 99th > model_profile.p99 * 1.8 for 60s -> TRIPPED.
Dependency-level thresholds (external routing, datastore): error-rate > 2% sustained 120s -> trigger model-specific fallback preferences and slow-rollback of retries.
Cooling policy: exponential backoff reconnection windows with minimum hold of 30s and max cool-down 15m; require two consecutive 'healthy' windows to reset to OK.
metrics_and_dashboards: Dashboard: SSB Overview - per-region/per-tenant trip counts, current states, and rollback rate (Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/s/ssb-overview)
Panel: Trip reason breakdown (latency | errors | token-surge | cache-miss)
Alert: TenantTripSpike P1 - a tenant hits HARD trip for >120s and >5% of total clusters capacity.
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (lab): unit tests + integration harness against fake backends (complete).
Stage 1 (canary): enable SSB in runtime for <1% of traffic across non-critical tenants in us-west1 for 48h. Monitor fallback QoR and Regressions. (target date: 2026-03-01).
Stage 2 (controlled ramp): expand to 10% traffic and include a small set of enterprise tenants behind feature flags for 72h. Verify SLA and cost delta.
Stage 3 (regional): enable region-wide for non-critical regions and observe multi-region failover interactions. Ensure fallbacks are region-compatible.
Stage 4 (global): full enable with auto-adjusted thresholds and complete observability; schedule a post-rollout review 2 weeks after full enable.
Rollback: global feature-flag to disable SSB immediately; per-tenant opt-out available via console.
testing_plan: Synthetic spike tests: ramp token throughput 10x for targeted tenants and ensure soft-trip engages within 60s and hard-trip within configured window.
Chaos test: introduce 503s on model endpoints and verify fallback selection and correct state transitions without cascades.
Quality gating: measure downstream generation quality (BLEU/semantic similarity proxy) for 100 sample prompts; require <7% degradation on average when fallback used.
Load soak: 6-hour run with mixed workload to validate cooling and reset semantics.
